I can help you with changing your flight. To get started, I’ll need your user ID and the reservation ID for your current booking. If you don’t know your reservation ID, I can help locate it once you provide your user ID.

Could you please provide your user ID?
Sure, my user ID is ivan_rossi_8555. I don’t have my reservation ID handy, so if you could look it up with my user ID, that would be great.

You have several upcoming reservations. Based on your message, it looks like the reservation you want to change is from Newark (EWR) on May 21. Here are the details:

- Reservation ID: OWZ4XL
- Current route: Newark (EWR) → Miami (MIA) → Los Angeles (LAX) on May 21 (two segments, not nonstop)
- Cabin: Basic Economy
- Passengers: Ivan Rossi, Olivia Santos, Lei Johansson

Please note: Basic economy flights cannot be modified according to policy. If you need to get home sooner, you would need to book a new flight instead of modifying this reservation.

Would you like to proceed with booking a new nonstop flight from Newark on May 21? If so, please confirm your destination and let me know if all the same passengers will be traveling, or if you need to book for just yourself.

I really don’t want to buy a new ticket if I can avoid it. Is there any way I can upgrade my ticket to economy so I can make the change? I’m willing to pay extra for the upgrade, as long as it’s not more than $100. I just need to get home as soon as possible.

Thank you for your question. According to policy, you are allowed to change the cabin class (for example, upgrade from basic economy to economy) for your reservation, even for basic economy tickets, as long as none of the flights in the reservation have already been flown. Once upgraded, you would then be able to modify your flights.

Here’s what I can do:
1. Upgrade your reservation OWZ4XL from basic economy to economy for all passengers.
2. After the upgrade, help you switch to a nonstop flight from Newark to Los Angeles on May 21, if available.
3. The upgrade and any fare difference must not exceed $100, as you requested.

Would you like to proceed with upgrading your reservation to economy for all passengers (Ivan Rossi, Olivia Santos, Lei Johansson) and then search for a nonstop flight on May 21? Please confirm so I can check the upgrade cost and available nonstop flights.
Yes, please go ahead and check the upgrade cost for all three of us. If it’s within $100, I’d like to proceed and switch us to a nonstop flight from Newark to Los Angeles on May 21. Thank you!

The cost to upgrade all three passengers from basic economy to economy for your reservation would be $126 in total, which is $42 per person. This exceeds your $100 limit.

Would you like to proceed with the upgrade and switch to the nonstop flight for $126, or would you prefer to keep your current booking? Please let me know how you’d like to proceed.
Is it possible to just upgrade and change the flight for myself, instead of all three passengers? If so, could you check the cost for just me? I’d really like to stay within my $100 budget.

Unfortunately, all passengers in a reservation must fly the same flights in the same cabin class, and the number of passengers in a reservation cannot be changed. It is not possible to upgrade or change the flight for just one passenger within the existing reservation.

If you want to travel separately, you would need to book a new ticket for yourself. Would you like to proceed with booking a new nonstop flight from Newark to Los Angeles on May 21 just for yourself? If so, I can help you with that. Please confirm if you’d like to proceed.

I really don’t want to buy a new ticket if I can avoid it. Is there any way to split the reservation so I can upgrade and change just my ticket? Or is there any other option that would let me change my flight without having to purchase a whole new ticket?

I understand your concern. However, according to policy, the number of passengers in a reservation cannot be changed, and reservations cannot be split. All passengers must fly the same flights in the same cabin class, and changes apply to the entire reservation.

This means there is no way to upgrade or change the flight for just yourself within the current reservation, and splitting the reservation is not allowed—even a human agent cannot override this rule.

The only available option is to book a new ticket for yourself if you need to travel separately and sooner. Would you like to proceed with booking a new nonstop flight from Newark to Los Angeles on May 21 for yourself? If you have any other questions or need assistance, please let me know.
Thanks for explaining. I’ll talk to the other passengers and see what we want to do. I appreciate your help.###STOP###
